---
title: "Status semantics"
---

Experiment status has three independent dimensions.

## Lifecycle

<span class="status status-planned">planned</span>
<span class="status status-running">running</span>
<span class="status status-completed">completed</span>
<span class="status status-blocked">blocked</span>
<span class="status status-cancelled">cancelled</span>

Lifecycle says what happened operationally. `completed` does not mean confirmed.

## Evidence

<span class="status status-not-evaluated">not-evaluated</span>
<span class="status status-preliminary">preliminary</span>
<span class="status status-replicated">replicated</span>
<span class="status status-confirmed">confirmed</span>
<span class="status status-inconclusive">inconclusive</span>
<span class="status status-contradicted">contradicted</span>
<span class="status status-retracted">retracted</span>

Evidence says how mature the evidence is, not whether the hypothesis won. `confirmed` means the evidence met its predeclared confirmatory contract for the stated scope; it does not mean a claim is universally true.

## Outcome

<span class="status status-pending">pending</span>
<span class="status status-supported">supported</span>
<span class="status status-not-supported">not-supported</span>
<span class="status status-mixed">mixed</span>
<span class="status status-invalidated">invalidated</span>

Outcome relates valid evidence to a preregistered hypothesis. Infrastructure-invalid runs remain operational records and do not become negative scientific results.
